claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation. Let me start with a few basics:

1. **How many children do you have or are responsible for?** (Please also let me know their names so I can keep track of each child's eligibility)

2. **Do you currently live in the UK?**

Let's start with these, and then I'll ask some follow-up questions about each child to properly assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit.

I have one child - Alex. And yes, I live in the UK.

What else do you need to know?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm glad to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some more questions about Alex:

**How old is Alex?**

This is important because the age rules are:
- Children under 16 automatically qualify (if other conditions are met)
- Children aged 16-19 may still qualify if they're in approved education or training

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 16 years old. He's still in school doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great - since Alex is 16 and in approved education (A-levels count as approved education), he can still qualify for Child Benefit.

Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's helpful to know.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One final question to complete my assessment:

**Have you or Alex recently moved to the UK from abroad, or do either of you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** 

(This helps me determine if there are any additional residency requirements to consider)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we haven't moved from abroad. We've been living here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

✅ **Alex is 16 and in approved education** - A-levels count as approved education, so you can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex until he turns 20 or leaves education/training, whichever comes first

✅ **Alex lives with you** - This establishes that you're responsible for him

✅ **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement

✅ **No one else is claiming** - Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and no one else is claiming for Alex

**Next steps:** If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. You should be able to make a successful claim.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
